notes: Date: 1 January 1291. The Ilkhan Arghun (d. 10 March 1291) rules Iran, Iraq and the overlordship of Anatolia, Georgia, Cilicia, the Kart of Herat and Kerman.

Anatolia: the Seljuk sultan Mesud II reigns at Konya under Ilkhanid governors. The Turkmen beyliks of 1291 are Karaman, Germiyan, Menteshe, the Sahib Ataids (Karahisar), the Pervaneids (Sinop), the Chobanids (Kastamonu), Ladik (Denizli) and the Eshrefids (Beyşehir). Osman's chieftaincy at Söğüt is tiny; Aydın, Saruhan, Karasi, Teke, Hamid, Candar, Eretna, Dulkadir and Ramadan of 1356 did not exist yet.
The Iranian successor states of 1356 (Jalayirids, Chobanids, Muzaffarids, Injuids, Sarbadars) and the Turkmen confederations of the Kara and Ak Koyunlu did not exist yet.
Hama is an Ayyubid principality under the Mamluks (al-Muzaffar III Mahmud, to 1299). Tripoli fell to the Mamluks in April 1289.

Maghreb: Marinids (Abu Yaqub Yusuf), Zayyanids of Tlemcen (Uthman I), Hafsids of Tunis (Abu Hafs Umar I) and of Bijaya and Constantine (Abu Zakariya, since 1285); Ceuta under the Azafids, nominally Marinid.
Jolof (founded c.1350 by tradition), Dulkadir and Ramadan are left out.

states.dynasty_note: Bahri Mamluk sultan since November 1290 (death of his father Qalawun on the march against Acre).

summary.en: Al-Ashraf Khalil has sworn to finish his father's work: Acre will be besieged in April.
summary.de: Al-Aschraf Chalil hat geschworen, das Werk seines Vaters zu vollenden: im April wird Akkon belagert.

coa.blazon: Or, a cup Gules between two inscriptions Sable

charges.text: Glory to our lord the Sultan

states.dynasty_note: The last Ayyubid principality, vassal of the Mamluks.
Sharifs of Mecca under Mamluk suzerainty; Medina has its own Husaynid emirs, attached here.
Rasulid sultan since 1250, at the height of the dynasty; took Zafar in Dhofar (1279).
Nabhani maliks of inner Oman; Qalhat and the coast stand under Hormuz.
The kings of Old Hormuz on the mainland (the move to Jarun island c.1300), tributary to the Ilkhan.
Ilkhan Arghun (1284-91), a Buddhist who sought an alliance with the Latin West against the Mamluks; he dies on 10 March 1291. Islam becomes the state faith only under Ghazan (1295).
Sultan since 1282/84 under Ilkhanid governors; real power lies with the Mongol officers and the Turkmen begs.
Karamanid beylik in the Taurus, at war with the Seljuks and the Ilkhanids.
The strongest beylik of the west, raiding the Byzantine frontier.
Turkmen beylik on the Carian coast; took Tralles from Byzantium (1282-84).
Descendants of the vizier Sahib Ata Fakhr al-Din Ali (d. 1288), lords of Afyonkarahisar (1275-1341).
The sons of the pervane Mu'in al-Din Süleyman (d. 1277) hold Sinop (1277-1322).

name.en: Beylik of the Chobanids of Kastamonu

states.dynasty_note: Frontier begs of Kastamonu since the early 13th century (the Candarids replace them c.1292-1309).
Turkmen lords of Denizli (Ladik), 1262-1368.
Lords of Beyşehir (1285-1326).
Osman, son of Ertuğrul, a frontier chief on the Bithynian border; the beylik is only counted from c.1299.
Kart maliks of Herat, vassals of the Ilkhan.
The Qara Khitai dynasty of Kerman under Ilkhanid overlordship (1222-1307).
Du'a, khan of the Chagatai ulus (1282-1307), the junior partner of Qaidu.
Qaidu, grandson of Ögedei, the paramount power of Central Asia and Kublai's enemy (1269-1301).
Marinid sultan since 1286; Algeciras, Tarifa, Gibraltar and Ronda are his Andalusian bridgeheads.
The Banu al-Azafi rule the trading city of Ceuta (1249-1327), recognising the Marinids.
Zayyanid sultan (1283-1304), besieged by the Marinids from 1299.
Hafsid caliph at Tunis (1284-95); the west of the realm (Bijaya, Constantine) has broken away under his nephew.
Separate Hafsid realm of Bijaya and Constantine since 1285.
The freed slave Sakura, a general who seized the throne (c.1285-1300), extends Mali to Gao.
Sayfawa kings of Kanem; ruler names around 1290 are uncertain.
Son of Yekuno Amlak, founder of the Solomonic dynasty (1270); reigns 1285-94.

coa.blazon: Vert, a lion Or bearing a cross

states.dynasty_note: The Walashma took Ifat and ended the Makhzumi sultanate of Shewa in 1285.
King Shemamun, fighting Mamluk-backed rivals for the throne of Dongola.
The Mahdali sultans (from c.1277) control the gold trade of Sofala.
Oba Oguola (c.1280-95), who walled Benin City by tradition.
